controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where K2 saw it dimmer (contrast drawn stronger) · December 2017 to February 2018, mapped in this project
controls.notes: HD 80653 in its own color, darker where its light in K2's images of December 2017 to February 2018 says it was darker. As the star turned once in 20.6 days its light rose and fell by 0.09%. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the eye can see it: the darkest part gives 0.6% less light than the brightest, and is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue; the Brightness map's scale has the measured values. The longitudes of the darker and brighter parts are measured. Their latitudes and shapes are not: they are the smoothest that reproduce the light. No change of color is drawn, because none is measured. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong.

controls.label: Brightness map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · K2 mission light curve, campaign 16
controls.notes: Where the star's surface was darker and brighter in K2 campaign 16, worked out in this project from how its light rose and fell by 0.09% as it turned once in 20.6 days. The light curve is the mission's own; the criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43) decide that it shows the star turning, and starry finds the map that reproduces it. The longitudes of the dark and bright regions are fixed by the data; their latitudes are not. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the star's mean surface; white: brighter.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from Gaia's spectrum of the star; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,959 K and log g 4.34 (u1 0.422, u2 0.282): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention.

physical.credit: Naponiello et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 80653 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive radius; Gaia DR3 astrometry; no measured rotation axis (display convention)
